record.paper_title: Conferences WORDS, years 1997-2017: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: ([2, Problem 1.10.9] generalized to arbitrary words): Can words generate arbitrarily large finite subtrees?

evidence.quote: ([2, Problem 1.10.9] generalized to arbitrary words): Can words generate arbitrarily large finite subtrees?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A$ be a finite alphabet and let $L \subseteq A^*$ be a language closed under taking prefixes (for example, the language of all finite words over $A$ that avoid a fixed pattern or fixed power). Order $L$ by the prefix relation: $u \le v$ iff $u$ is a prefix of $v$. The Hasse diagram of $(L, \le)$ is a rooted tree $T(L)$ whose nodes are the words of $L$ and whose root is the empty word. For $w \in L$, let $T_w(L)$ denote the subtree of $T(L)$ consisting of all extensions of $w$ that lie in $L$; we say that $w$ generates $T_w(L)$.

Fix a finite word $p$ over some alphabet, and let $L_p$ denote the language of all finite words over a chosen finite alphabet $A$ that avoid $p$ as a factor (i.e., no factor of any word in $L_p$ is an instance of $p$, in the appropriate sense of pattern avoidance for words).

Question: For a general (arbitrary) word $p$, can $L_p$ contain words $w$ that generate arbitrarily large finite subtrees $T_w(L_p)$? Equivalently, is the supremum, over all $w \in L_p$ such that $T_w(L_p)$ is finite, of $|T_w(L_p)|$ infinite?
artifact.status_search_result: The question, originating from Petrova and Shur in the context of prefix trees of power-free / pattern-avoiding languages, has follow-up work on branching densities of cube-free and square-free words (Petrova–Shur, 2021), but no source located resolves the generalized question for arbitrary words. Status appears unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Branching Densities of Cube-Free and Square-Free Words
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses the structure of prefix trees in cube-free words and related open problems by Petrova and Shur.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work by the proposers continues to study the prefix-tree structure but does not announce a resolution of the arbitrary-word generalization.

status_evidence.title: Ten Conferences WORDS: Open Problems and Conjectures
status_evidence.snippet: Lists the question of whether words can generate arbitrarily large finite subtrees as an open problem from the WORDS conferences.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is listed in the compendium of open WORDS conference problems.
